title: 1.1 Limits of Functions Using Numerical and Graphical Techniques

icans: I can use a table to investigate a limit.
I can use a graph to find one-sided limits and decide whether a limit exists.
I can describe the slope of a tangent line as a limit of the slopes of secant lines.

vocab: lim f(x) = L as x → c means f(x) gets as close to L as we like by __________ x close enough to c, x ≠ c
the ____________ limit (x → c⁻) and the right-hand limit (x → c⁺)
the ___________ position of the secant lines through P = (c, f(c)) and a point Q on the graph as Q moves closer to P

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Limit: f(x) gets as close to L as we like by taking x close enough to c, but x _______________ c.

blocks.stem: Use a table to investigate the limit of (x² − 4)/(x − 2) as x → 2.

notes: The value at c does not matter: the limit as x → c does not depend on f(_______________); f can even be undefined there.
titles: The value at c does not matter

blocks.stem: f(x) = x + 1 for x ≠ 2, and f(2) = 5. Find the limit of f(x) as x → 2 and f(2).

notes: One-sided limits: the limit as x → c is L if and only if both one-sided limits _______________ L.

blocks.stem:
Find the limit at c, if it exists.
a.  f(x) = 2x + 5 if x ≤ 2;  4x + 1 if x > 2;  c = 2
b.  f(x) = 2x + 1 if x ≤ 0;  2x if x > 0;  c = 0
Use a table (radians) to investigate the limit of (sin x)/x as x → 0.

notes: Slope of the tangent line: m_tan = the limit as x → c of (f(x) − f(c))/(x − c), the limit of the slopes of _______________ lines.

blocks.stem: f(x) = 3x². Find the slope of the secant line through (2, 12) and (x, 3x²), then the slope of the tangent line at (2, 12).
f(x) = x² if x < 1;  2x + 3 if x ≥ 1. Find the one-sided limits at 1 and the limit, if it exists.

(AP® Practice) The limits of f(x) as x → 3⁻ and as x → 3⁺ are both 5, and f(3) = 2. Which is true?
(A) The limit of f(x) as x → 3 is 2.   (B) The limit of f(x) as x → 3 is 5.
(C) The limit of f(x) as x → 3 does not exist.   (D) f(3) = 5

tickets.stem: The left-hand limit at c is 4 and the right-hand limit at c is 6. Does the limit exist?
Can the limit of f(x) as x → c exist if f(c) is undefined?
